page: Microsoft Azure DC2as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DCasv6 series, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built upon dedicated x86_64 AMD processor hardware, allocating 2 dedicated vCPUs alongside 8.0 GB of system memory. This yields a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio of 4.0 GB per core, standard for general compute needs across cloud workloads.

The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or integrated graphics accelerators, remaining dependent on external network-attached volumes such as Azure Premium Storage. Furthermore, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. From an architectural standpoint, the instance trades local ephemeral high-speed IOPS for remote storage reliability and configuration flexibility.

Given its two-core footprint and modest memory allocation, the DC2as_v6 provides a cost-efficient profile for small-scale production systems or development environments that require isolated compute resources without the overhead of massive memory capacity or specialized GPUs. Typical deployment targets include lightweight web servers, background service workers, microservices, and small relational or key-value data storage setups.

It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The hardware footprint presents an entry-tier dedicated compute profile, delivering qualitative cost efficiency for resource-constrained services. Typical workloads appropriate for this server type include microservices, development environments, lightweight backend services, and small caching or database layers.
